analysis: The arrival of fats and/or solutions with low pH to the duodenum triggers the release of hormones like secretin and cholecystokinin (CCK). Secretin is released in response to low pH to stimulate the pancreas to secrete bicarbonate, neutralizing the acid. CCK is released in response to fats to stimulate the gallbladder to release bile and the pancreas to release digestive enzymes. Both secretin and CCK work to slow gastric emptying to allow for proper digestion and absorption in the small intestine. Therefore, the arrival of fats and/or low pH solutions to the duodenum reduces gastric emptying.
